Dizer o que dói, passo a passo: Saying what hurts, step by step
PASSO 1: para dizer o que DÓI, use «weht: STEP 1: to say what HURTS, use «wehtun» (separable) with the DATIVE of the person: «Der Kopf tut mir weh» (my head hurts — literally "the head does me pain"). STEP 2: plural: «Die Füße tun mir weh» (my feet hurt). STEP 3: ask «Was tut Ihnen weh?» or «Wo tut es weh?» (Where does it hurt?). STEP 4: another way, with «-schmerzen» (aches), just like English "headache", "stomachache", "backache": «Ich habe Kopfschmerzen / Bauchschmerzen / Halsschmerzen / Rückenschmerzen» (a sore throat = Halsschmerzen). STEP 5: «Es tut weh» means "it hurts", with no person. STEP 6: remember the dative reflexive from lesson 38: «Ich habe mir die Hand verletzt» (I hurt my hand) — German says "the hand", not "my hand". Very common in the Perfekt.
O dativo vem logo depois de «tut»; «weh»: The dative comes right after «tut»; «weh» goes to the end.

PASSO 1: para os sintomas, use «haben»:: STEP 1: for symptoms, use «haben»: «Ich habe Fieber» (I have a fever — no article!), «Ich habe Husten» (I have a cough), «Ich habe eine Erkältung» (I have a cold). STEP 2: the doctor gives instructions in the formal IMPERATIVE (lesson 13): «Trinken Sie viel Tee», «Bleiben Sie im Bett», «Nehmen Sie die Tabletten dreimal täglich.» STEP 3: dosage: «einmal / zweimal / dreimal täglich» (once / twice / three times a day), «vor dem Essen» (before meals), «nach dem Essen» (after meals). STEP 4: at the pharmacy: «Ich hätte gern etwas gegen Kopfschmerzen» (I'd like something for a headache) — English "for" becomes «gegen» (against) + accusative. STEP 5: «Ich brauche ein Rezept» (I need a prescription) and «Haben Sie ein Rezept?» (Do you have a prescription?). False friend: «Rezept» means prescription (or recipe), never "receipt" (that's «die Quittung»).

Marcar uma consulta, passo a passo: Making an appointment, step by step
PASSO 1: para marcar: «Ich möchte einen: STEP 1: to make one: «Ich möchte einen Termin vereinbaren» (I'd like to make an appointment). STEP 2: the receptionist suggests: «Haben Sie am Dienstag um zehn Uhr Zeit?» (Are you free on Tuesday at ten?) STEP 3: you accept or suggest another time: «Ja, das passt mir gut» (that works for me) or «Leider nicht. Geht es am Mittwoch?» (Unfortunately not. Does Wednesday work?) STEP 4: confirm: «Dann sehen wir uns am Dienstag um zehn Uhr.» STEP 5: if you need to cancel: «Ich muss meinen Termin leider absagen» (unfortunately I have to cancel my appointment). Note: «Termin» is any appointment; a "date" in the romantic sense is «ein Date».

— A senhora está resfriada. Fique três d: — You have a cold. Stay in bed for three days and drink lots of tea.
— Preciso tomar comprimidos?: — Do I need to take pills?
— Sim, tome os comprimidos três vezes ao: — Yes, take the pills three times a day after meals. Here's the prescription.
